title: Magnetic wire proposals
summary: Move a node close enough and a dotted proposal draws itself — gated by BOTH a per-port magnet radius and a data-type check, tracking the drag live, ranked nearest-first with a deterministic tie-break, and vanishing the moment you leave range. Prior art was read on disk (JointJS, maxGraph, React Flow, SystemSketch) and the 'break it into regions' question was settled by measurement, not by argument.

findings: GATES, measured before and after in this worktree. typecheck: clean -> clean. unit (pnpm exec vitest --project=unit run): 550 passed (30 files) -> 611 passed (33 files), +61 mine. stories (pnpm test-stories): 229 -> 235, +6 mine.

PRE-EXISTING FLAKE, not mine: on the untouched lane tip, `DragPolicy.stories.tsx > Block (simple/port/value) - the whole face grabs` failed one baseline run and passed the next, in isolation, with my files moved out of the tree. Measured deliberately before touching anything. The final full run was 53 files / 235 tests green.

THE GATES ARE NOT VACUOUS — mutation-tested red twice. (1) Swapping the scan to React Flow's ordering (pick the nearest, THEN judge it) turned 8 unit tests and 2 story tests red, including TypeDecides. (2) Deleting the two identity rungs from the tie-break turned 3 unit tests red, including the 100-shuffle determinism test. Both mutations reverted.

THE CAPTURE SCRIPT FOUND A BUG THE PLAY FUNCTIONS COULD NOT. Its first run photographed four empty canvases: each story's own play function AUTOPLAYS on load and leaves the bench committed elsewhere (and RadiusAndToggle leaves magnets OFF), and a reload just replays it. That is invisible to a play function, which never inspects the bench it inherits. Fixed by adding a Reset control to the bench — which is also simply what you want after dragging a node into a corner.

TWO MORE FIXES CAME FROM LOOKING AT THE PICTURES, not from a test: a real mouse drag across a Block header text-SELECTS it (synthetic dispatched events never reproduce this), fixed with userSelect:none; and with `show="all"` every candidate was painting `hinting`, which is a small lie — `hinting` means 'this port is previewing becoming wired', and exactly one is. Now only the winner hints.

R2's refusal is now visible ON THE CANVAS, not only stamped in an attribute — Zach: 'if you would release it would error... Drag time validity preview!'. The readout reads `refused: sink/in many-to-one` while the pointer is still down, and the story asserts that before the release rather than after it.

NOT VERIFIED IN-APP UNDER ZOOM. DomCanvas has no viewport by design and its own tripwire says a story needing pan/zoom moves to the React Flow bench. effectiveMagnetRadius's zoom rule is covered by unit test A1 only, where it is asserted EQUAL to hitRegions/hitPolicy.ts's effectiveHitValue at every zoom stop, so the reuse is mechanical rather than decorative.

DEMONSTRATED ON A STORY-LOCAL BENCH, NOT THROUGH THE REAL HOST. PortEdgeItem carries no `hinting` and nodeViews.tsx has no per-port hook, so eligible-port paint cannot travel through DomCanvas today; both files are another lane's write set. Lint.stories.tsx hit the identical wall for the identical reason. That gap is real and is owed wiring, not something this report should gloss.

OWED MERGE, named rather than papered over: magnetTypeJudge is exported so the linter lane can absorb it as an at-rest `type-mismatch` rule. If that lane ships its own type rule concurrently, there will be two judges and the merge is owed.

sections.heading: The prior-art answer, first — because it is the question that was asked
sections.html:
Zach asked two things directly: “check prior art jointjs, maxgraph, etc”, and “computation wise to avoid being KNN I think maybe you can break it up into regions.” Everything below was opened on disk or fetched this run. Nothing is cited from memory.

What the libraries actually do for this exact query

LibraryIts broad phaseIts ordering: geometry vs. validity
JointJS (MIT core)findClosestMagnetToPoint → findCellViewsInArea → Graph._filterInArea, which bottoms out in cells.filter(el => rect.intersect(el.getBBox())) — a linear scan over every cell, then a second scan over every [magnet] node on each survivor. _markAvailableMagnets does not even bbox-prefilter.Interleaved. The distance scan takes a filter callback and the gate is isBetterCandidate && (!filterFn || filterFn(view, magnet)) — an illegal nearer magnet is skipped, not chosen-then-rejected.
maxGraph (Apache-2.0)Zero region-partitioning structures anywhere. A full-tree grep of all 1189 paths for quad/rtree/spatialindex/kdtree/hash-grid returns nothing; getCellAt/getCells are recursive rectangle-intersection scans.Its getEdgeValidationError contract is three-valued (null / '' silent / a message) — the shape this lane's ConnectionVerdict already had.
React Flow @xyflow/system@0.0.82 (installed here)getNodesWithinDistance is a for…of over nodeLookup.values() with an AABB pre-filter inflated by a hardcoded ADDITIONAL_DISTANCE = 250 (index.mjs:2367-2386).Nearest first, THEN validate. getClosestHandle (:2387-2419) runs to completion, and isValidHandle (:2618) only flips a flag on the already-chosen candidate. Under this order Zach's own example fails whenever the wrong-type port is nearer.
SystemSketchLinear scan over getCurrentPageShapesSorted() with a per-shape bounds±radius reject (blockPorts.ts:516-560).Interleaved, and it says so: “An illegal dot never shadows a legal one behind it: refusal is judged per candidate, in distance order” (connectionRules.ts:337-360).

So: no spatial index. Zach's second guess was right; the first was wrong at our n

Grid-vs-linear was measured, not argued: the crossover sits at n≈500-1000, and our regime is tens to low hundreds of ports. At ten times our regime (~5,000 ports) a plain linear scan still costs ~6-8 µs per frame — 0.05% of a 16.6 ms budget. Four mature libraries ship brute force for the identical query. Shipping an index would add a real bug class (cell-iteration order leaking into tie ordering, boundary straddling) for zero measured gain.

What the arithmetic actually costs was never the problem — getBoundingClientRect was. That is the one optimization this lane ships: the resting geometry is measured from the DOM exactly once, on pointer down, and the moving ports are derived from dragDelta. A scanning frame performs zero DOM reads. That also removes the render storm there would otherwise be something to rAF-throttle away — and with no rAF in the loop, every play function's post-pointermove assertion is deterministic instead of racy.

rbush (an MIT R-tree already present transitively via tldraw) was the strongest off-the-shelf candidate and is rejected on access pattern, independently of scale: its value is cheap online mutation, and our resting set is frozen for the whole gesture. If an index is ever genuinely needed the upgrade is a uniform grid, not a tree. A // WHY: comment on scanMagnets carries the crossover so a future reader does not “fix” this into a grid.

The one decision that changes the product

We take SystemSketch's and JointJS's interleaved order over React Flow's. It is not a style preference: under React Flow's order, “it would only connect to the port with the correct datatype” is false whenever the wrong-type port is nearer — which is precisely the example Zach wrote. The TypeDecides fixture therefore puts the wrong-type sink strictly nearer, and the play function measures and asserts that before asserting the outcome, so the fixture cannot rot into the easy case and a builder reaching for the more familiar library's order fails a test instead of shipping a green lie. Mutation-tested: making the swap turns 10 tests red.

sections.heading: Seen mid-gesture, under a real mouse
sections.html: These are not story screenshots. docs/capture_magnet_shots.mjs presses with page.mouse (real CDP input, real pointer capture), glides, and screenshots without lifting — because a magnet proposal only exists while a pointer is down. Each capture also reads the live DOM at the moment of the shot and records it, so a capture cannot silently become a picture of nothing. The facts quoted in each caption are from that run.

images.title: R4 · the type decides, not the distance
images.caption: `bytesSink/in` is measurably NEARER and is skipped; the dotted proposal reaches past it to `poseSink/in` at 77.2u. Observed at capture: proposals=1, to=poseSink/in, refusals=`bytesSink/in:type-mismatch`, strokeDasharray=`0.1px, 6px`. Under React Flow's ordering this picture would show nothing at all.

images.title: R3 · in range, tracking the drag
images.caption: Observed at capture: proposals=1, distance=80.00, from-at=`321,209`, to-at=`401,209`. The from-point moves with the dragged node and the to-point does not — which is what the story asserts, at ±1px, against the node's own `getBoundingClientRect` delta.

images.title: R3 · out of range, mid-drag, pointer still down
images.caption: Same gesture, dragged away: proposals=0 and zero `[data-magnet-proposal]` nodes. The story then drags back in and asserts the SAME `data-magnet-id` returns — the id is derived from the port pair, never minted, so a proposal that leaves and comes back is the same proposal.

images.title: R5 · ranked nearest-first, with an exact tie
images.caption: Four legal candidates, every proposal drawn. `alphaTie/in` and `zetaTie/in` are measured at exactly 104.40 each; `midway` 120.00, `outer` 216.33. The tie resolves to the smaller port key — a deliberate divergence from all three libraries studied, every one of which breaks ties by array/enumeration order and would therefore change its answer when the candidate list is rebuilt (which it is, every frame). Proved by shuffling the input 100 times and demanding a byte-identical result.

images.title: R1 · per-port magnet radius, drawn
images.caption: The dragged port declares a deliberately tiny 10u magnet so the CANDIDATES decide. At 80.0u from both, `small`'s 40u circle visibly does not reach and `big`'s 120u circle does. Swap the two numbers with the on-canvas control and the proposal flips — same geometry, different declaration. Per-port radius is OURS: JointJS's `snapLinks.radius` and maxGraph's `graph.tolerance` are both single global scalars.

images.title: R2 · in range, type-correct, and still refused
images.caption: `producer/out` already feeds `sink/in` (the solid wire). Dragging `src` into range gets no proposal — and the reason is on the canvas: `refused: sink/in many-to-one`, from `scene/edgeValidation.ts`'s landed `validateConnection`, reached through the same one-line `ConnectionJudge` seam as the type gate. Proximity and validation are both required, and the story measures that it really is inside the radius first, so 'no proposal' cannot be a proximity failure dressed up as a rule.

sections.heading: Off-the-shelf vs. hand-rolled, element by element
sections.html:
ElementToday / naiveThe stock part used, by its exact exported nameBehaviour that must survive
The dotted lineA second renderer with its own strokeDasharrayTrace with variant="delayed" (components/trace.tsx) — its traceStrokeStyle already returns {strokeDasharray: "0.1 6", strokeLinecap: "round"}, and TRACE_VARIANT_LABELS.delayed is literally "Dotted", Zach's own wordThe proposal's geometry and a real wire's geometry stay identical by construction. Owed upstream: `delayed` is a semantically wrong name for a transient proposal; a future reader will assume a magnet proposal IS a delayed connection. `trace.tsx` is another lane's write set, so this is borrowing, marked at the seam.
The zoom rule for a screen-px radiusRe-typing px / zoom locallyeffectiveHitValue(px, zoom, "screen") (hitRegions/hitPolicy.ts:51) — this is its second consumer and first real one; an audit found zero hosts using itOne spelling of the zoom rule in the app. Unit test A1 calls both functions and compares at every zoom stop, so the reuse is mechanical, not decorative.
Press → drag intent, threshold, cancelA new pointer state machineuseDragIntent / dragDelta / thresholdFor (interaction/) — composed, never replacedThe delta is measured from the ORIGIN, not the threshold crossing (React Flow loses the first move's travel permanently). Magnet geometry inherits that correctness free, and Escape still rolls the whole gesture back in one step.
The structural rules (dangling / self / many-to-one)A second rule engine inside the magnet modulevalidateConnection (scene/edgeValidation.ts:102), reached through a structural ConnectionJudge callback — never imported by the module itselfThree lanes are writing src/scene/ concurrently. A rename over there costs ONE line in the story, not a rebuild. `ConnectionVerdict`/`ConnectionMessage` are type-only imports; `Diagnostic` is deliberately never named, because post-rename it lives in the fenced `components/highlighter.tsx`.
The data-type comparisonInventing a matching rulearePortTypesCompatible / normalizePortType / WILDCARD_PORT_TYPES, ported from SystemSketch connectionModel.ts:138-166Case- and whitespace-insensitive, for the donor's own stated reason (a port's type is text a person typed on a whiteboard). Two refusal codes, not one — `type-mismatch` and `untyped-port`, the donor's own pair.
The dev radius overlayNew colour tokensHIT_REGION_FILL / HIT_REGION_LINE (components/hitRegion.ts)A magnet circle reads as the same class of dev chrome as a hit region — one visual language, no new tokens.
Unchanged (stock seam)—Block, Port, Toggle, WireLayer's resolveDot/centreOf technique, DomCanvas, registry.json, package.jsonDeliberately not touched. `Port`'s existing `hinting` prop is what paints the winner; no component was edited to make this feature work.
Rejected off-the-shelf partA spatial indexrbush (MIT R-tree, already a transitive dep via tldraw) — and kdbush/flatbush, quadtrees, sweep-and-pruneNamed rather than left unconsidered: rbush IS the textbook-correct structure for a 2D window query. Rejected on access pattern (its value is cheap online mutation; our resting set is frozen for the gesture) and on the measurement above. Zero dependencies added.

sections.heading: What is left, and what needs you
sections.html:
Done and proved

  • R1 per-port radius + toggle — unit A1 (zoom stops, cap, commutativity over 100 seeded pairs) and story A10 (the radii decide; swapping them flips the answer; magnets off still drags the node).
  • R2 proximity AND validation — unit A2 (a spy judge's call count equals the in-range count, so an out-of-range candidate provably never reaches validation) and story `RefusalPreview` (a real `many-to-one` from the landed engine).
  • R3 dotted, tracking, vanishing — story A7/A8/A9, with the dash read off `getComputedStyle` rather than inferred from the variant prop.
  • R4 type filtering — unit A4/A5 and story A6, with the wrong-type sink measured strictly nearer first.
  • R5 nearest wins, deterministic ties, no index — unit A3 (100 shuffles, byte-identical) plus the measurement in §1.

Left, and merely next (not blocked)

  • Wire it through the real host. `PortEdgeItem.hinting?: boolean` + forwarding in `nodeViews.tsx` is the whole change; both files are another lane's write set today. Until then this is proved on a story-local bench.
  • Zoom in-app. Needs the React Flow bench, per `DomCanvas`'s own tripwire. Unit-tested only right now.
  • Absorb `magnetTypeJudge` into the linter so at-rest boards can be linted for type mismatches too. Exported and ready; the linter lane's call.

Needs you — with the default I will take if you say nothing

  • Is 48u the right default magnet? It is ours, ad hoc — sanity-checked against React Flow's 20 flow units and SystemSketch's 13 screen px, deliberately larger than a hit target because it fires while you are still moving. Default if you say nothing: leave it at 48 and tune from the stories.
  • Should the winner be the only thing drawn? Right now yes, with “Show all proposals” as an opt-in. Default if you say nothing: keep top-only.
  • Should a refused candidate's own line be drawn in red rather than not drawn? maxGraph does exactly this (it shifts the dragged preview edge's stroke green 3px / red 1px). Not what you described, so it is not built. Default if you say nothing: leave refusals to the port dimming plus the on-canvas reason.

Deliberately not done

  • Any spatial index — measured unnecessary at our n and at 10× it; four mature libraries ship none.
  • Caching judge verdicts at drag start — rejected on correctness, not cost: `ConnectionJudge` is a caller-supplied callback whose type promises nothing about position-independence, so caching would silently break a position-dependent judge.
  • A `variant:"proposed"` on `Trace`, a `type-mismatch` rule in `lint.ts`, and any edit to `src/scene/scene.ts` — all in other lanes' write sets.
  • Any dependency. `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` are untouched.
